title: Jude and the House
premise: Xanthe Villalobos takes a teaching post at Hollowmere Academy, where students vanish one desk at a time and the staff pretend not to notice. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the school's oldest wing, Xanthe recognizes the scratching she has heard for fifteen years — the house has been waiting for someone who would finally listen. As night falls, she discovers the school was built as an invitation, and the last resident's signature is all that remains to complete it. To survive until sunrise, Xanthe must refuse to sign, unmake her own complicity in the disappearances, and accept that belonging to the house means becoming its next door.
about_author: Mirabel Vasquez is a former night-shift archivist who spent years cataloguing the belongings of people no one came to claim. She writes horror about institutions that remember more than they admit, and lives somewhere with very thick walls.

chapters.title: First Bell
chapters.summary: Xanthe Villalobos arrives at Hollowmere Academy for her first day, noting the empty desks and the way colleagues flinch at the word 'transferred.' POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: uneasy optimism masking fifteen years of learned denial.

chapters.title: The Attendance Problem
chapters.summary: A student named Wren asks Xanthe why the school keeps enrolling kids who were never there. The registrar's ledger shows names crossed out in wet ink. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: the first crack in her practiced rationalism.

chapters.title: Scratching
chapters.summary: Alone grading papers after dark, Xanthe hears the familiar scratching inside the walls and tells herself, as always, pipes. A chalkboard fills with tally marks matching her fifteen years. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: dread of being recognized by something patient.

chapters.title: Colleagues Who Don't Blink
chapters.summary: Vice-Principal Okafor warns Xanthe never to answer knocking after the last bell. In the faculty lounge, portraits of former teachers have faces worn smooth from touching. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: isolation; everyone knows and no one will say.

chapters.title: Wren's Map
chapters.summary: Wren gives Xanthe a hand-drawn map of the school marking rooms that 'aren't there on Thursdays.' One room is circled twice: the old west wing, closed since 1974. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; hope is dangerous here.

chapters.title: The Excavation
chapters.summary: Crews break ground behind the west wing and unearth a stone door — scratched, dented, sealed from the inside. The foreman quits before lunch. That night the scratching stops for the first time in fifteen years. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: silence worse than sound.

chapters.title: Sealed From Within
chapters.summary: Xanthe examines the door and finds fingernail grooves on the inner face. Someone locked themselves in to keep something out — or themselves in with something. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: vertigo of realizing her whole life rhymes with this place.

chapters.title: The Last Resident
chapters.summary: In the archive, Xanthe finds the deed: Hollowmere was willed to 'whoever stays.' The final page holds a signature line, blank for fifty years, and a photograph of a teacher with Xanthe's face. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: identity begins to dissolve.

chapters.title: Thursday
chapters.summary: It is Thursday. The west wing exists again. Xanthe walks it with Wren and finds classrooms mid-lesson, decades old, dust suspended like held breath. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: awe curdling into grief for everyone absorbed.

chapters.title: What Was Invited
chapters.summary: Okafor confesses: the founders invited something in to save the town from famine, paying in children, renewed each generation by a resident's signature. His own name is second-to-last on the deed. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: horror of inherited complicity.

chapters.title: Roll Call
chapters.summary: At morning attendance, Xanthe reads aloud names of the missing and every empty desk answers. Wren doesn't come to class. Her desk is warm. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: guilt made physical; the price is being collected now.

chapters.title: Negotiating With Walls
chapters.summary: The house speaks through intercom static and heating vents, offering a trade: sign, and Wren returns. It shows Xanthe memories of her childhood home — which was also Hollowmere's floor plan. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: temptation; belonging offered as a weapon.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Explanations
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: young Xanthe fleeing a house that scratched, telling herself stories ever since. She realizes she didn't find Hollowmere; it recruited her. POV: Xanthe (past and present braided). Emotional beat: the cost of survival was never looking.

chapters.title: Doors
chapters.summary: Xanthe finds doors throughout the school that open onto the same small room — the inside of the buried door. Someone carved HELP on the far side, then scratched it out. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: claustrophobic empathy with whoever sealed themselves in.

chapters.title: The One Who Stayed
chapters.summary: In the Thursday wing, Xanthe meets the 1974 teacher, half-absorbed into the walls, still refusing to sign. She explains the rules: the house cannot hold what refuses to belong. Then she loses her face mid-sentence. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: terror and instruction in one breath.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Sunset. The school seals itself. Corridors rearrange; exits open onto classrooms. Okafor signs to save his daughter and is taken mid-stroke, pen still moving. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: despair; every escape route is an invitation.

chapters.title: Wren, Found
chapters.summary: Xanthe reaches Wren in the buried chamber behind the door, alive but translucent, being measured for a desk. The house offers the deal again, sweeter now, using Wren's voice. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: love weaponized; the climax's stakes made flesh.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Xanthe takes the pen and instead of signing, writes her own name on the list of the missing — claiming them, not the house. The deed burns. The walls scream in fifteen years of accumulated voices. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: defiant self-sacrifice; identity reclaimed by giving it away.

chapters.title: Unmaking
chapters.summary: The house tries to keep her by becoming her memories — her mother's kitchen, her first classroom. Xanthe walks through each, naming them as past, refusing to stay. The buried door swings open onto ordinary dirt. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: exhausting liberation; you leave by admitting you were kept.

chapters.title: Sunrise Roll Call
chapters.summary: Dawn. Students return, including Wren, solid and confused. The missing of fifty years do not — but their desks are gone too, released. The west wing is rubble. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: bittersweet accounting; survival tallied honestly.

chapters.title: Resignation Letter
chapters.summary: Xanthe submits her resignation, but stays through the term because leaving the children mid-year would be another kind of signing. Okafor's office stands empty, his daughter enrolled elsewhere, safe. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: quiet responsibility; belonging chosen, not imposed.

chapters.title: New Walls
chapters.summary: Months later, in a small apartment with thin, honest walls, Xanthe hears scratching — a branch, just a branch — and lets herself believe it. On her doorstep: a blank deed, unsigned, waiting. She burns it and sleeps. POV: Xanthe. Emotional beat: vigilance without surrender; the price of survival, paid ongoing.
